questions.q: Why should Investigation 1 (the balanced-journal check) normally return zero rows, unlike most of this course's exception checks?
options: Because journals are never actually balanced in real data
Because GL_JE_LINES never contains any rows
Because HAVING cannot be used with SUM comparisons
Because a valid accounting journal always has total debits equal to total credits by definition — a nonzero result signals a serious problem
questions.explain: Double-entry accounting requires every journal to balance; finding an imbalanced journal would indicate a serious data integrity issue, not a routine exception.

questions.explain: CLOSING_STATUS tracks a period's state (e.g., open, closed, permanently closed), which is essential to check before processing transactions into it.

questions.q: Why is checking whether a period is open before processing transactions considered an important guardrail?
options: It has no real importance in practice
Processing into a period assumed to be open without checking can lead to posting into the wrong period or a closed period, corrupting the close
Oracle Fusion always prevents this automatically with no check needed
GL_PERIODS never changes its closing status
questions.explain: Never assuming a period's status avoids accidentally posting transactions into a period that's already closed or not yet open for the intended activity.

questions.q: In Investigation 3, what does `ABS(c.net_activity - NVL(p.net_activity, 0))` compute?
options: The sum of both periods' net activity
Only increases, ignoring any decreases
The absolute value of the swing between current and prior period net activity, regardless of direction
The average of current and prior period net activity
questions.explain: ABS() ensures that both large increases and large decreases in net activity are treated as equally significant swings worth investigating.

questions.q: Why does Investigation 3 use two separate CTEs (current_period and prior_period) rather than one?
options: To cleanly compute each period's net activity independently before comparing them in the outer query, each with its own period_name filter
CTEs cannot filter by different WHERE conditions
Because GL_BALANCES cannot be queried more than once in a single statement
There is no reason — a single CTE would work identically
questions.explain: Each CTE isolates one period's net activity with its own filter, making the comparison in the outer query clear and avoiding repeated, hard-to-read filtering logic.
